nodes.text: 1. Form 3 of Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers-Disclosure scheme will be enabled shortly

2. Due dates for filing of Income Tax Returns and Audit Reports for AY 2026-27 are extended in the cases of persons mentioned at Sl.No.2 in the Table below Explanation2 to Sub-section (1) of Section 139 of Income Tax Act 1961 vide Circular No.07/2026 dated 28th September,2026.
3. Form 1 under the “Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers Disclosure Scheme” is now available for filing.
4. ITR-1, ITR-2, ITR-3, ITR-4, ITR-5, ITR-6 and ITR-7 for AY 2026-27 are available for filing through both online and offline utilities.
5. Filing of TDS/TCS Correction Statements pertaining to Tax Year 2026-27 has been enabled.

6. Demand Management Facilitation Centre (DFC), has been set up to guide Taxpayers on issues/grievances regarding their outstanding demands. DFC may be contacted through the e-mail id: taxdemand@cpc.incometax.gov.in or on the toll-free number - 1800 309 0131 or chargeable no. 0821-6671200.
7. Excel utilities for filing Updated return for ITR-1 to 7 for AY 2022-23 as per Finance Act, 2026 are available for filing !

A  involves examining a taxpayer’s books, GST returns, invoices, and other records to verify compliance with GST requirements. It helps identify discrepancies in turnover, tax liability, input tax credit (ITC), and other reporting matters.

A GST officer may conduct an audit of a registered person under the applicable provisions of the GST law. The audit generally covers books, returns, turnover, exemptions, tax rates, ITC, refunds, and other relevant records.
A special audit may be directed where the prescribed conditions are met and examination of the taxpayer’s records by a Chartered Accountant or Cost Accountant is considered necessary.

Eligible taxpayers crossing the prescribed turnover threshold are required to furnish , a reconciliation statement comparing information reported in the GST annual return with the audited annual financial statements. The applicable requirements should be checked for the relevant financial year.
The audit or review is initiated under the applicable GST provisions.
Where required, the taxpayer receives an audit notice and is asked to provide relevant records.
Books, invoices, GST returns, ITC claims, turnover, and other records are examined.
Financial records are compared with GST returns and reported transactions.
Discrepancies, if any, are communicated to the taxpayer for clarification or response.
Audit findings are finalized after considering the taxpayer’s response.
